title: CS 4535: The Ticket Hunt
description: Due Wed Sep 16, 23:59 ET. File the issues and post the triage comments on GitHub first, then record them here. We dedupe, size and label from this form on Sep 16–17, and what survives becomes the cs4535-first-ticket pool published Thu Sep 17.
completedHtml:
Recorded.

The triage gate runs Sep 16–17. The cs4535-first-ticket pool is published Thu Sep 17, and project bids are due that night at 23:59 ET.

pages.name: ticket1
pages.title: Ticket 1: the student role
pages.description: Pawtograder used as yourself, on the coursework you actually have, in this course or any other.

elements.name: t1_url
elements.title: Link to the issue you filed

validators.text: Paste the full URL of an issue on pawtograder/platform.

elements.name: t1_labeled
elements.title: The issue carries the cs4535-hunt label

validators.text: Add the cs4535-hunt label to the issue, then check this. We find your work by that label.

elements.name: t1_search_terms
elements.title: What terms did you search before filing?
elements.description: Open and closed issues both. Duplicate filing is the most common way this assignment goes wrong.
elements.placeholder: e.g. gradebook column group slug, gradebook grouping, column header split

elements.name: t1_affects
elements.title: Who does this affect?

elements.name: t1_scope
elements.title: How many of them?
elements.description: This is what decides whether anybody picks the ticket up.

choices.text: One person with an unusual setup
Some users, under a particular configuration or course setup
Everyone in a course that hits this workflow

elements.name: t1_where
elements.title: Where did you see it?

elements.name: t1_seed
elements.title: What did you seed?
elements.description: The seed options you ran, so somebody else can reach the same state.
elements.placeholder: e.g. npm run seed with FIXED_GRADER_EMAIL set to my address

elements.name: t1_evidence
elements.title: What evidence is attached to the issue?
elements.description: Something beyond your own account of events.

elements.name: t1_why
elements.title: One sentence on why it matters
elements.description: Whose week is worse for this, and how. Name the mechanism if you found it.

validators.text: A sentence, not a phrase. Name the role and what the defect costs them.

elements.name: t1_size
elements.title: How big is the fix?
elements.description: A size estimate is not a commitment, and "I can't size it" is a legitimate answer.

choices.text: An hour or two for somebody who knows the area
Bigger than that, or it needs a design decision first
I can't size it, and here's what I'd need

elements.name: t1_cannot_size
elements.title: What would you need to size it, and who has it?

elements.name: t1_reproduced
elements.title: I made this happen myself, and the steps in the issue are the steps I ran

validators.text: A filed ticket needs a reproduction you performed. If you can't make it happen, it's a hypothesis, and hypotheses go to Discord.

pages.name: triage
pages.title: Two items you triage
pages.description: Somebody else's records, not your own findings from this week. Each verdict is a comment on the item itself.

elements.name: triages
elements.title: Triage verdicts

templateElements.name: source
templateElements.title: Where did the item come from?

choices.text: A TODO comment in the tree
An open issue with no label and no size

templateElements.name: item_url
templateElements.title: Link to the item you triaged
templateElements.description: The issue, or a permalink to the line carrying the TODO.

validators.text: Paste the permalink to the comment you posted.

choices.text: No longer real: fixed, obsolete, or a false positive
Undecidable without something I don't have

templateElements.name: reasoning
templateElements.title: How you reached it
templateElements.description: The specifics a reader can check: the commit that introduced the TODO, the ship date of the migration it refers to, the line showing the branch is unreachable, the screen-reader output. "Still relevant" earns nothing.

validators.text: Cite something checkable. This is the part we're grading.

choices.text: An hour or two for somebody who knows the area
Bigger than that, or it needs a design decision first
I can't size it, and here's what I'd need

templateElements.name: blocked_on
templateElements.title: What you'd need, and who has it
templateElements.description: Name it precisely. "I need to know whether phase 2 is scheduled, and only the instructor knows" is both correct and useful.

templateElements.name: not_mine
templateElements.title: This is somebody else's record, not something I found this week

validators.text: A verdict on something you reproduced an hour ago can only come out "still real." Pick an item somebody else recorded.

pages.name: wrapup
pages.title: The rest of what you found
pages.description: Optional, except for the last question. This is where the pool gets its reserve and where we find out whether the assignment was the size we thought it was.

elements.name: unfiled
elements.title: Anything you found and didn't file
elements.description: Smaller than a ticket, out of scope, or you ran out of week. One line each is fine.

elements.name: unreproduced
elements.title: Anything you couldn't make happen twice
elements.description: Post these in Discord too, where somebody may help you confirm them.

elements.name: hours
elements.title: Roughly how many hours did the whole assignment take you?
elements.description: Including setup, the four roles, filing and triage. This is how we size next year's version of the assignment.
